I traced the 403 to the namespace list authorization path. [ListNamespaceRequest.Request](/app/rpc/flipt/request.go:106) creates a read request with an empty namespace. The [authorization interceptor](/app/internal/server/authz/middleware/grpc/middleware.go:70) passes it through `IsAllowed`, so a policy that requires a named namespace denies the list before it reaches the endpoint.

The likely fix spans four places: add `Namespaces` and `NamespacesKey` in [authz.go](/app/internal/server/authz/authz.go); evaluate `viewable_namespaces` in both [bundle](/app/internal/server/authz/engine/bundle/engine.go) and [rego](/app/internal/server/authz/engine/rego/engine.go) engines; put the result in request context in the interceptor; and filter the list and total count in [namespace.go](/app/internal/server/namespace.go:22). The fix should cover the specified role combinations, empty results, malformed decisions, and pagination. Pagination behavior after filtering needs particular care.

I updated [.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). **No project source or tests were changed**, and I did not run tests; this task’s specialist instructions limited my work to diagnosis.

Implemented namespace-aware listing. Both authorization engines now evaluate `viewable_namespaces`; the interceptor passes accessible namespaces to the service, which filters results before calculating the count and pages. Added coverage for the requested role combinations, invalid decisions, and pagination.

`go test ./internal/server/authz/... ./internal/server -count=1` and `git diff --check` pass.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** The API patch filters the namespace list, but the UI does not redirect an unauthorized namespace route. [Layout.tsx](/app/ui/src/app/Layout.tsx:43) leaves `/namespaces/default/...` in place after the list loads, while [namespacesSlice.ts](/app/ui/src/app/namespaces/namespacesSlice.ts:21) initializes the selection to `default`. A user with access only to `local` can therefore still reach pages that request `default` and receive 403 errors. After loading the list, select an accessible namespace and replace an unauthorized route, while preserving valid deep links.

**Tests:** `go test ./internal/server/authz/... ./internal/server -run 'Test(Engine_Namespaces|Engine_IsAllowed|AuthorizationRequiredInterceptor|FormatNamespaces|ListNamespaces)' -count=1` exited 0. The relevant authz, bundle, rego, middleware, and server tests passed.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** None.

Fixed the reviewed UI defect in [Layout.tsx](/app/ui/src/app/Layout.tsx). Once the namespace list loads, valid deep links remain in place; an unauthorized namespace route is replaced with an accessible namespace’s Flags page before its content mounts. The UI also shows a message when the list is empty.
